overall: The AG found the regional Hamilton-Wenham Capital Management Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting notice in Wenham under 48 hours before its June 15, 2011 meeting and never posting notice in Hamilton; advisory status did not excuse notice.

allegations.summary: Notice of the June 15, 2011 meeting was allegedly posted in Wenham fewer than 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee posted notice for its June 15, 2011 meeting in Wenham fewer than 48 hours before the meeting.

allegations.summary: Notice was allegedly never posted in Hamilton, the other town the regional committee serves, and the notice was not transmitted to the Hamilton Town Clerk.
allegations.key_passage: The lack of posted notice in Hamilton also constituted a violation of G.L. c. 30A, § 20(c).

allegations.summary: Committee argued it is an advisory body with no authority and took no action at the meeting, so posting was unnecessary; the AG rejected this defense.
allegations.key_passage: However, that does not excuse the Committee from posting notice in compliance with G.L. c. 30A, § 20.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
